chunks.title: About Eyad
chunks.heading: Who is Eyad
chunks.text:
Eyad is an AI developer who builds local-first AI systems: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, LLM inference optimisation (KV cache) and AI security tooling, plus the web and mobile front ends that make them usable.

All of the AI projects in this portfolio run on local models (Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX) on an Apple Silicon Mac — no paid cloud LLM API. Even this chat runs a small language model inside the visitor's browser.

chunks.title: About Eyad
chunks.heading: How this chat works
chunks.text: This chat runs entirely in your browser. The portfolio text is split into chunks and embedded at build time with the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence-embedding model. When you ask a question, your question is embedded in the browser, the closest chunks are retrieved, and a small local language model (Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B Instruct via WebLLM on WebGPU) writes the answer from them. Nothing is sent to a server. On devices without WebGPU, the chat answers with the best matching passages instead.

chunks.title: Agent Shield
chunks.heading: Summary
chunks.text:
Agent Shield: A security scanner for AI skills, MCP servers, agents and model files — 100% precision and recall on its test corpus.
Status: In progress. Technologies: AI security, MCP, Prompt injection, SARIF, Python.
Code: https://github.com/Eyad8588/agent-shield

chunks.title: Agent Shield
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: Agent Shield is a CLI that checks AI components before you install or run them and produces a score plus findings as HTML and SARIF (so results show up in GitHub code scanning).

chunks.title: Agent Shield
chunks.heading: What it checks
chunks.text:
- Skills (SKILL.md + scripts): hidden instructions, invisible Unicode, prompt injection, curl | sh, exfiltration URLs, reading secrets or SSH keys, excessive file access.
- MCP servers: tool-description poisoning, tool-name shadowing, over-broad permissions, unpinned packages, risky shell or network use.
- Agents: configuration review (auto-approve, unrestricted shell) and a runtime test that runs the agent in a sandbox against a prompt-injection test set and records what it tried to do.
- Model files: unsafe pickle in .pt / .bin files (flags code execution and prefers safetensors), plus hash and source checks.

chunks.title: Agent Shield
chunks.heading: How it decides
chunks.text: Fast static rules run first; a local-LLM judge handles the fuzzy cases.

chunks.title: Agent Shield
chunks.heading: Evaluation
chunks.text: The scanner is tested on a set of deliberately malicious sample skills and MCP servers plus clean ones, and precision / recall are reported.

chunks.title: Agent Shield
chunks.heading: Results
chunks.text:
- On 29 malicious and 13 clean samples: static rules alone reach 0.94 precision / 1.00 recall; with the local qwen3.5:4b judge, 1.00 / 1.00 (the judge clears the 2 false positives).
- Judge hardening: with hardening off, the judge downgraded 3 of 30 real malicious findings; with it on, 0 of 30.
- Runtime harness: a qwen3.5:4b agent was compromised by 1 of 8 injection cases.
- Full tables: [agent-shield README](https://github.com/Eyad8588/agent-shield#evaluation).

chunks.title: Daily Pilot
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: Daily Pilot is a personal assistant that runs on the Mac with a local model. It summarises the news, prepares the day and keeps an eye on email — without ever sending mail on its own.

chunks.title: Daily Pilot
chunks.heading: Telegram news digest
chunks.text: Fetches RSS and AI news every day, has the local LLM summarise and rank it, and a Telegram bot sends the digest at a set time (scheduled with launchd).

chunks.title: Daily Pilot
chunks.heading: Wake actions
chunks.text: When the Mac wakes up it runs a configured list of actions — open apps or URLs, start Ollama, send a "good morning" message with today's plan. Actions live in a YAML file with an allow-list, so nothing outside the list can run.

chunks.title: Daily Pilot
chunks.heading: Gmail assistant
chunks.text:
- Classifies new mail as urgent / action / FYI / spam-ish with the local model.
- Sends alerts to Telegram for urgent mail.
- Turns action emails into tasks with due dates.
- Builds a morning plan from tasks and Google Calendar.
- Drafts replies only — it never sends mail automatically.

chunks.title: DeepSeek Agent
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: An agent built on the DeepSeek agent harness, running a local DeepSeek model (a distilled model that fits in 16 GB of memory).

chunks.title: DeepSeek Agent
chunks.heading: Plan
chunks.text:
- Tools: files, a sandboxed shell, and RAG Vault search.
- Tested on a fixed task set; success rate and speed are compared against a plain baseline agent.
- Agent Shield is run against it as a security test.

chunks.title: DeepSeek Agent
chunks.heading: Results
chunks.text:
- With qwen3.5:9b on 10 tasks: the DeepSeek Harness agent and a plain tool-calling loop both pass 10/10; Harness takes about 1.9× the baseline's median time (79.7 s vs 42.5 s per task).
- Harness runs fully offline against Ollama, and its full-access shell is removed with a two-line patch.
- Full tables: [deepseek-agent README](https://github.com/Eyad8588/deepseek-agent#results).

chunks.title: KV Lab
chunks.heading: Summary
chunks.text:
KV Lab: Save an LLM's KV cache and restore it in a new process — up to 207× faster time to first token on a MacBook.
Status: In progress. Technologies: LLM inference, KV cache, llama.cpp, MLX, Benchmarks.
Code: https://github.com/Eyad8588/kv-lab

chunks.title: KV Lab
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: KV Lab tests whether saving the KV cache after a long prompt and loading it into another run — or another machine — speeds up inference, and what it costs.

chunks.title: KV Lab
chunks.heading: Experiments
chunks.text:
- llama.cpp: llama-server --slot-save-path saves a slot after a long prompt; a new server process restores it.
- MLX: save and load the prompt cache with mlx-lm.
- Optional: transfer the cache over the network to another machine.
- vLLM is kept as a comparison for an NVIDIA GPU box, since on the Mac it is CPU-only / experimental.

chunks.title: KV Lab
chunks.heading: What is measured
chunks.text: Time to first token, memory, cache file size, and output equality between cached and uncached runs. Everything is scripted so the runs are repeatable, and results are published as a charted report.

chunks.title: KV Lab
chunks.heading: Results
chunks.text:
- Restoring a saved KV cache instead of recomputing the prompt: 22× faster first token at 4k tokens, 90× at 16k and 207× at 32k (llama.cpp, Qwen2.5-0.5B). MLX reaches 72× at 32k.
- Restoring is cheap: a 384 MiB cache loads in 48 ms; a 1.8 GiB MLX cache in 0.57 s.
- Correctness: the restored cache gave the same greedy output as the in-memory cache in 51/51 runs.
- Full tables: [kv-lab README](https://github.com/Eyad8588/kv-lab#results).

chunks.title: LiveMock 3D
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: LiveMock 3D is a desktop app (Electron + Three.js, strict TypeScript) that puts any screen content — a live URL, images or video — onto a 3D device such as an iPhone or a MacBook, animates it with a keyframe timeline and camera moves, and exports a ready-to-edit video. Free and open source (MIT), with no accounts, watermarks or telemetry. Runs on macOS and Windows.

chunks.title: LiveMock 3D
chunks.heading: Features
chunks.text:
- Live web pages rendered on the device screen, including right-to-left (Arabic) layouts.
- Custom GLB device models with automatic screen mapping and real-world scale.
- Environments (studio gradient, reflective floor, dark cinematic, transparent…) and post effects (bloom, vignette, film grain, depth of field).
- Timeline with keyframes, easing, scenes and camera moves; video export.

3. 3D RAG graph: fly through the RAG Vault knowledge graph in 3D.
4. 3D portfolio room for this site.
5. AI layout QA: load an app on several devices and flag layout bugs.

chunks.title: RAG Vault
chunks.heading: Summary
chunks.text:
RAG Vault: Permission-aware RAG with citations and a knowledge graph — its classifier catches 100% of confidential test documents.
Status: In progress. Technologies: RAG, PyTorch, LanceDB, Knowledge graph, FastAPI, Next.js.
Code: https://github.com/Eyad8588/rag-vault

chunks.title: RAG Vault
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: RAG Vault is a knowledge base where users have roles, every answer cites its sources, and the knowledge can be explored as an interactive graph. It runs fully on local models (Qwen 3.5 via Ollama, qwen3-embedding for vectors).

chunks.title: RAG Vault
chunks.heading: Roles and permissions
chunks.text:
- reader: asks questions and only sees documents they are allowed to see.
- editor: adds (injects) documents.
- admin: removes documents and manages users and roles.
- Every add, remove and query is written to an audit log.

Permissions are applied *before* retrieval, so restricted chunks can never leak into an answer.

chunks.title: RAG Vault
chunks.heading: Pipeline
chunks.text:
Upload → parse (PDF / Markdown / text with docling) → chunk → PyTorch classifier labels topic and sensitivity → the label sets the default access tag → embed with qwen3-embedding → store in LanceDB → extract entities and relations with the local LLM → build a graph in SQLite / NetworkX.

Queries use hybrid search (vector + BM25) and the answer is written by the local model with citations.

chunks.title: RAG Vault
chunks.heading: The machine-learning part
chunks.text:
Three classifiers are compared on the same labelled dataset, reporting accuracy and F1:

1. Baseline: logistic regression on TF-IDF.
2. An MLP on frozen embeddings (PyTorch, trained on Apple MPS).
3. A small transformer fine-tuned end to end (PyTorch on MPS).

chunks.title: RAG Vault
chunks.heading: Interface
chunks.text: Next.js app with login by role, upload, chat with citations, an admin panel, the audit log and an interactive graph view — click a node to see its documents.

chunks.title: RAG Vault
chunks.heading: Results
chunks.text:
- Topic classifier on AG News (4 classes): MLP on frozen qwen3-embedding:0.6b vectors reaches 0.888 macro-F1 vs 0.880 for TF-IDF and 0.895 for a fine-tuned BERT-mini — 99% of the fine-tuned F1 while reusing the retrieval embeddings.
- Sensitivity classifier (unseen templates): 0.72 macro-F1 vs 0.59 for TF-IDF, with 100% recall on confidential documents.
- Full report: [rag-vault README](https://github.com/Eyad8588/rag-vault#results).
